items.title: Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.content_snippet: Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Web Answer is a managed tool that returns a synthesized, grounded, cited answer to a natural-language question in a single call, so agent builders can attach it to an agent and get back a finished answer grounded in current web sources, without building and maintaining their own search, retrieve, synthesis, and citation pipeline. items.content_snippet: AWS Network Load Balancer is now available in the Phoenix Local Zone (us-west-2-phx-2a). items.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces the general availability of bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB, a fully managed feature that writes data from Amazon S3 into your existing DynamoDB tables. Many DynamoDB applications use data that other systems produce and store in Amazon S3. Writing this data into existing DynamoDB tables has typically meant building custom pipelines and managing table capacity. items.content_snippet: Starting November 1, 2026, the Amazon Cognito Service Level Agreement (SLA) commits to a Monthly Uptime Percentage of 99.99% for user pools on the Plus feature plan, up from 99.9%. User pools already on Plus are automatically covered by the new Service Commitment. User pools on Essentials and Lite stay at the 99.9% Service Commitment with no change to their terms. items.title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports automatic certificate revocation checking
items.content_snippet: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports automatic revocation checking using certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution points (CDPs). This helps keep revocation checks in sync with your certificate authority (CA) and can help improve your security posture. items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine now supports agent traces
items.content_snippet: Today, the Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine adds support for agent traces, including OpenTelemetry traces. Your traces and logs now live in the same place. You can follow a request or an agent session from start to finish, find the step that failed or slowed down, and check the related logs without switching tools.
